entry: [[Species]] of [[Fly|fly]] (*Musca domestica*) in the family Muscidae, spread worldwide as a commensal of humans. The species possibly originated in the Middle East. Adults are gray to black, with four dark longitudinal lines on the [[Thorax|thorax]] and a single pair of membranous [[Wing|wings]]. Females usually mate once and store the sperm. They lay batches of about 100 eggs on decaying organic matter such as food waste, carrion or feces. The eggs hatch into legless white larvae, or maggots, which become [[Pupa|pupae]] after two to five days. Adults normally live two to four weeks and can hibernate in winter. Houseflies carry [[Pathogen|pathogens]] on their bodies and in their feces and contribute to food-borne illnesses such as typhoid fever, so they are considered pests. Their short life cycles have made them useful in laboratory research on aging and sex determination.

Group of one or more people who live in the same dwelling, which may be a single [[Family|family]] or another type of group. Households are the basic unit of analysis in many social, microeconomic and government models, and are important to [[Economics|economics]] and [[Inheritance|inheritance]]. Household types include blended families, shared housing, group homes and houses of multiple occupancy (UK) or single room occupancy (US). The U.S. Census counts all persons who occupy a housing unit as one household, including unrelated roommates. In [[Sociology|sociology]], household work strategy, coined by Ray Pahl in his 1984 book *Divisions of Labour*, describes how members divide work. [[Feminism]] examines how gender roles shape that division.

Most populous city in [[Texas]], in Southeast Texas near the [[Gulf of Mexico]] (pop., 2020: 2.3 million). Founded by land investors on August 30, 1836, it was named after [[Sam Houston]], president of the [[Republic of Texas]]. The city grew from a 19th-century trading center into a port and railroad hub, and the Texas oil boom fueled further expansion. Mid-century, it became home to the Texas Medical Center, the world's largest concentration of healthcare and research institutions, and NASA's Johnson Space Center, home to Mission Control. The Port of Houston ranks first in the United States in international waterborne tonnage. The city has the second-most Fortune 500 headquarters of any U.S. municipality and has become a [[Global city|global city]], with strengths in culture, medicine and research.

Amphibious craft, also called an air-cushion vehicle (ACV), that travels over land, water, mud, ice and other surfaces. Blowers force a large volume of air below the hull, creating a cushion slightly above [[Atmospheric pressure|atmospheric pressure]] that lifts the craft. Air is typically blown through slots or holes around a disk- or oval-shaped platform, giving most hovercraft a rounded-rectangle shape. Unlike ground-effect vehicles and hydrofoils, hovercraft can lift while stationary. Very large versions carried hundreds of people and vehicles across the [[English Channel]], while military models transport tanks and soldiers. As of 2025, only two year-round public hovercraft services remain in the world: Hovertravel, between the [[Isle of Wight]] and Southsea in the UK, and Oita Hovercraft in Japan.

American film director, producer and screenwriter of the classic Hollywood era. Hawks worked across comedies, dramas, gangster films, science fiction, film noir, war films and [[Western (genre)|Westerns]]. His popular films include *Scarface* (1932), *Bringing Up Baby* (1938), *Only Angels Have Wings* (1939), *His Girl Friday* (1940), *The Big Sleep* (1946), *Red River* (1948) and *Rio Bravo* (1959). He was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Director for *Sergeant York* (1941) and later received an honorary Academy Award. His frequent portrayals of strong, tough-talking women defined the "Hawksian woman". His influence reached directors including [[Martin Scorsese]], [[John Carpenter]], [[Quentin Tarantino]] and [[Clint Eastwood]]. [[Jean-Luc Godard]] called him "the greatest of all American artists".

American aviator, aerospace engineer, business magnate and film producer. Hughes first became prominent in Hollywood with big-budget films such as *Hell's Angels* (1930) and *Scarface* (1932). In 1932 he founded Hughes Aircraft Company, and over the next two decades he set multiple world air speed records and built landmark planes, including the H-1 Racer (1935) and the H-4 Hercules (1947), known as the Spruce Goose and the largest flying boat in history. He acquired and expanded Trans World Airlines. Hughes won the Collier Trophy (1938) and the Congressional Gold Medal (1939) for his aviation achievements. In later years his eccentric, reclusive lifestyle was caused partly by [[Obsessive–compulsive disorder|obsessive–compulsive disorder]], chronic pain from a near-fatal plane crash and deafness. In his final years he extended his business empire to [[Las Vegas]], where he is largely credited with transforming the city into a more refined, cosmopolitan place.

American broadcaster, comedian and media personality. Stern is best known for *The Howard Stern Show*, which was syndicated nationally on radio from 1986 to 2005 and has been broadcast on SiriusXM since 2006. In 2004 he signed a five-year, $500 million deal with Sirius. The Federal Communications Commission issued $2.5 million in fines to station owners over the show's indecent content. His books *Private Parts* (1993) and *Miss America* (1995) debuted at number one on the [[The New York Times|New York Times]] bestseller list. From 2012 to 2015 he was a judge on *America's Got Talent*.

Canadian comedian, actor, television personality and producer. Mandel voiced Gizmo in the film *Gremlins* (1984) and played Dr. Wayne Fiscus on the [[NBC]] medical drama *St. Elsewhere*. He created and starred in the Fox children's cartoon *Bobby's World*, and he hosted the game show *Deal or No Deal* on NBC and later CNBC. He has been a judge on *America's Got Talent* since 2010. He was one of the first VeeJays on [[Nickelodeon]]'s music video series *PopClips*. He has also received a star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]].

[[Artillery]] piece between a [[Cannon|cannon]] and a [[Mortar (weapon)|mortar]], capable of both low-angle and high-angle fire. Howitzers fire explosive shells and incendiary materials into fortifications, and they can be used in battery formations with long-barreled guns and rocket artillery. The English word derives from the Czech *houfnice*, a short-barreled cannon used by the [[Hussite Wars|Hussites]]. By the early 20th century, howitzers were classified as field, siege, super-heavy siege and defense types. They played major roles in [[World War I]] and [[World War II]], especially in trench warfare. Modern howitzers are often self-propelled, mounted on tracked or wheeled vehicles.

Uninhabited coral island and nature reserve just north of the [[Equator|equator]] in the central Pacific Ocean. An unincorporated territory of the United States, it is managed as a wildlife refuge by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. It is best known as the island [[Amelia Earhart]] and Fred Noonan were trying to reach when they disappeared on July 2, 1937, during their round-the-world flight. The island was mined for [[Guano|guano]] in the 19th century and colonized in the 1930s. It has no fresh water, and it is primarily a nesting habitat for [[Seabird|seabirds]].

Indian actor and film producer who works primarily in Hindi cinema. He has won six Filmfare Awards, four of them for Best Actor, and is known for his dancing and varied characters. His breakthrough leading role came in *Kaho Naa... Pyaar Hai* (2000). He starred in the science fiction film *Koi... Mil Gaya* (2003) and its superhero sequels, *Krrish* (2006) and *Krrish 3* (2013). He played Mughal emperor [[Akbar]] in *Jodhaa Akbar* (2008) and a quadriplegic in *Guzaarish* (2010). He is one of the highest-paid actors in India.

Centrally governed city in central [[Vietnam]], formerly Thừa Thiên Huế province, on the South China Sea. Historically part of Thuận Hóa, a territory that [[Champa]] ceded to Đại Việt in 1306 as a wedding dowry, Huế became the provincial capital in 1687 and the capital of Vietnam under the [[Nguyễn dynasty]] from 1802 to 1945. The city was the administrative capital of the Nguyễn dynasty and later the capital of the French protectorate of Annam. Its [[World Heritage Site|UNESCO-designated]] complex of palaces, tombs and temples includes the Imperial City, the Forbidden Purple City and temples on its outskirts. Huế has 128 km of coastline and over 200,000 ha of forest.

Chinese politician, general secretary of the [[Chinese Communist Party]] (2002–2012) and president of China (2003–2013). Trained as an engineer at [[Tsinghua University]], Hu rose through party posts before becoming the presumed successor to [[Jiang Zemin]]. His government expanded national healthcare coverage and responded to the 2008 Sichuan earthquake and the 2009 [[Ürümqi]] riots. The Anti-Secession Law, which set conditions for military force toward unification with [[Taiwan]], passed during his tenure. His administration is described as technocratic and cautious in political reform. He retired voluntarily from all posts, succeeded by [[Xi Jinping]].

Legendary folk heroine of the [[Northern and Southern dynasties]] era (4th to 6th century CE). According to legend, Mulan took her aged father's place in [[Conscription|conscription]] by disguising herself as a man. After prolonged service against nomadic tribes beyond the northern frontier, she declined high office and asked only for a horse to return home. She revealed herself as a woman after 12 years of service, to the astonishment of her comrades. The earliest known record is "The Ballad of Mulan", a folk song believed to date from the Northern Wei dynasty (386–535 CE). Some evidence suggests she may have been Xianbei rather than [[Han Chinese]], since the Northern Wei were ruled by the Xianbei. Her story was later recounted in the 17th-century novel *Romance of Sui and Tang*, but she is absent from *Exemplary Women*, so her historicity is unclear.

Chinese salt trader and soldier who led a major rebellion against the [[Tang dynasty]] and proclaimed himself emperor of the Qi dynasty in 881. From Yuanqu, in present-day [[Shandong]], his family had long been salt smugglers, and he repeatedly failed the imperial examinations before rebelling. He joined Wang Xianzhi's rebellion in the mid-870s, split from Wang, and conquered [[Guangzhou]]. In 881 his troops captured the Tang capital Chang'an, forcing Emperor Xizong to flee. Huang reigned for almost four years, but Tang forces led by the Shatuo chieftain Li Keyong defeated him in 883, and he fled Chang'an. He was reportedly killed by his nephew Lin Yan, though the reports are inconclusive. The rebellion severely weakened the Tang dynasty.

Chinese multinational technology company based in [[Shenzhen]], making telecommunications equipment and consumer electronics. Founded in 1987 by Ren Zhengfei, a former officer of the [[People's Liberation Army]], it surpassed Ericsson in 2012 to become the world's largest telecommunications equipment manufacturer. Concerns that its equipment could enable [[Espionage|espionage]] for the Chinese state have led several countries to restrict it; Huawei says its critics have shown no evidence of espionage. It settled intellectual property claims brought by [[Cisco]]. In 2022 the U.S. Federal Communications Commission banned sales or imports of Huawei equipment on national security grounds.

Space telescope in [[Low Earth orbit|low Earth orbit]], launched in 1990 by NASA with contributions from the [[European Space Agency]]. Named after astronomer [[Edwin Hubble]], it observes in the ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared regions of the [[Electromagnetic spectrum|electromagnetic spectrum]] from above Earth's atmosphere. Its 2.4 m mirror was ground incorrectly, causing spherical aberration that was corrected during a 1993 servicing mission. Hubble is the only telescope designed to be maintained in space by astronauts, and five [[Space Shuttle]] missions repaired and upgraded it. Its observations have led to breakthroughs such as determining the rate of [[Expansion of the universe|expansion of the universe]]. It is predicted to last until 2030 to 2040, and the [[James Webb Space Telescope]] is its infrared successor.

Observation in [[Physical cosmology|physical cosmology]] that galaxies recede from Earth at speeds proportional to their distance. A galaxy's recessional velocity is typically measured from its [[Redshift|redshift]]. Officially the Hubble–Lemaître law, it is attributed to [[Edwin Hubble]]'s work published in 1929, after [[Georges Lemaître]] had concluded in 1927 that the universe might be expanding. The proportionality constant is the Hubble constant, measured in km/s/Mpc: a galaxy 1 megaparsec (3.09×10¹⁹ km) away recedes at 70 km/s. The law is considered the first observational basis for the [[Expansion of the universe|expansion of the universe]] and supports the [[Big Bang]] model.

Province in central China, with its capital at [[Wuhan]]. It has the seventh-largest economy among Chinese provinces and the third-largest among inland provinces. Its name means 'north of the lake', referring to Dongting Lake. The territory was part of the powerful State of Chu during the [[Spring and Autumn period]], and the Qin and Han later extended farmland here and maintained river dikes against summer floods. Hubei borders [[Henan]], Anhui, Jiangxi, [[Hunan]], [[Chongqing]] and Shaanxi. The [[Three Gorges Dam]] lies at Yichang in the west of the province, while the Jianghan Plain grows [[Rice|rice]] and cotton.

Large body of saltwater in northeastern [[Canada]], described as an inland marginal sea of the [[Arctic Ocean]]. At 1,230,000 km2 (470,000 sq mi), it is the second-largest water body called a bay, after the [[Bay of Bengal]]. Its average depth is about 100 m. The bay is named after Henry Hudson, who explored it in 1610. Its drainage basin covers about 3,861,400 km2 across parts of Nunavut, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario, Quebec, Manitoba and several northern U.S. states. Fur trading at the bay led to the creation of the [[Hudson's Bay Company]].

River in eastern [[New York (state)|New York]] that forms part of the border with [[New Jersey]]. It flows 315 miles (507 km) south from the Adirondack Mountains to New York Bay. Its lower half is a tidal [[Estuary|estuary]] occupying a [[Fjord|fjord]] carved by glaciers. The river was named after Henry Hudson, an Englishman who explored it in 1609 while sailing for the [[Dutch East India Company]]. The Erie Canal, completed in 1825, linked Albany with Buffalo on [[Lake Erie]]. The river inspired the Hudson River School of [[Landscape painting|landscape painting]]. Industrial contamination from PCBs grew in the mid-20th century, and restoration projects have begun to improve water quality.

Canadian holding company of department stores, founded by royal charter in 1670 and liquidated in 2025. Chartered by [[Charles II of England|King Charles II]], it held a trading monopoly over Rupert's Land and dominated the [[Fur trade|fur trade]] until it relinquished control of the land to Canada in 1869. It then ran department stores, including the Hudson's Bay chain, and acquired Zellers in 1978. The company filed for creditor protection in March 2025, closed its stores by June 2025, and sold its intellectual property to Canadian Tire. Its liquidation was essentially complete by December 2025.

English actor known for romantic comedies and later for character roles. Grant won a Golden Globe and a BAFTA Award for Best Actor for *Four Weddings and a Funeral* (1994), and followed it with *Notting Hill* (1999). He won the Volpi Cup for Best Actor for *Maurice* (1987). He later took character roles in *Paddington 2* (2017) and *Heretic* (2024). He received two Primetime Emmy Award nominations, for *A Very English Scandal* on the [[BBC]] and *The Undoing* on [[HBO]]. He was a prominent critic of [[Rupert Murdoch]]'s News Corporation during the News International phone hacking scandal.

American magazine publisher and businessman who founded *Playboy* in 1953. The first issue featured [[Marilyn Monroe]], who was not paid for the photographs. The magazine combined sexualized photographs with articles, fiction and lengthy interviews with politicians, musicians, artists and writers. Hefner extended the brand into a world network of Playboy Clubs. He lived in luxury mansions where Playboy Playmates shared his partying lifestyle, which fueled media interest.

Australian and British actor, singer and producer, best known for playing [[Wolverine (character)|Wolverine]] in the [[X-Men]] films. He played the character across the [[Marvel Cinematic Universe]], from *X-Men* (2000) to *Deadpool & Wolverine* (2024). His leading film roles include *The Prestige* (2006), *Real Steel* (2011) and *The Greatest Showman* (2017). For playing Jean Valjean in the musical [[Les Misérables (musical)|Les Misérables]] (2012), he was nominated for the [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] for Best Actor and won a Golden Globe. He won a Tony Award for *The Boy from Oz* (2004) and has hosted the Tony Awards four times.
